command: ./gather_designs 500 21 64 16  (steps, trials, GEMVs per trial, weight matrices)
device: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition
nvidia_smi: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, driver 595.91.07, max SM clock 3090 MHz
conditions: shared GPU, default (time-sliced) compute mode; another tenant held ~52 GB and 20-45% utilisation. Micro trials were kept to ~1 ms (500 boundaries) so most trials run inside one time slice: min and median agree within 1% for almost every design, and two full fp32 runs agree within 1-2% (1b_counter_data varied 1.64-1.94 us across earlier development runs).

method.micro: persistent kernel, one 256-thread block per SM (64 KiB dynamic smem pad forces 1 block/SM; cooperative launch for co-residency, cluster launch for 4x/5b). At every boundary each SM writes its slice (~22 words) of a V-word activation vector and must then hold the whole vector before writing the next slice. Every element of every step is checked against a value that encodes the step. ns per boundary = kernel time / 500 boundaries; min and median over 21 trials. V = 4096 fp32 words (16 KiB) or, with -DVW=2048, 8 KiB (the same 4096 hidden as bf16). The LL16/LL128 layouts keep one 128 B line per producer, so their vector is 24 KiB in both builds.
method.gemv_chain: Qwen3-8B 4096x4096 bf16 GEMV, fp32 activations, 188 blocks, 64 dependent GEMVs per trial cycling over 16 matrices (512 MiB, 4x L2: every weight byte comes from DRAM). Weights stream into a shared-memory ring of 8 KiB rows by TMA (cp.async.bulk + mbarrier) or per-thread cp.async. exposed ns per boundary = per-GEMV time of the dependent chain minus the stream-only kernel of the same structure (paired per trial, 11 trials, variants interleaved). 256 rows of every GEMV checked against a double-precision host reference (max rel err 1.2e-8).

l2_hit_latency_cycles_single_thread.note: 256 KiB pointer chase; varies by process with where the buffer lands (near vs far L2 partition): 354-358 cycles in the final runs, 412-870 in development runs; dep_latency_v2 measured 680-835. The per-design min_l2_round_trips field uses the run value (~355 cycles), so read it as near-L2 trips.

checks: 1a_counter_only 659 ns = 1,899 cycles, reproduces dep_latency.cu (663 ns): ~2 L2 traversals plus 188 serialised same-line atomics
reading a ready 16 KiB vector costs 377-401 ns = ~1,100 cycles: one far-L2 round trip (~700-870) + 16 KiB at ~64 B/clk (256); 8 KiB: 176-209 ns
one shared copy read by all 188 SMs: 614 ns (hot lines on few L2 slices); 8 replicas: 377 ns; private copies: 401 ns -- replication removes the hot spot
gather with data = signal + data + the fence waiting for the data stores to be acknowledged: 659 + 377 + ~200 = ~1,230 ns (3d_sharded1_rep8, 1,233 measured)
GEMV stream 1,598-1,621 GB/s vs 1,601-1,760 GB/s for a plain read kernel on the same buffer: the chain is DRAM-bound; 32 MiB / 1.6 TB/s = 21 us per GEMV, measured 20.7-21.0 us

DSMEM on this part: cluster.sync + 16 KiB peer read = 2,290 ns, 8 KiB = 1,233 ns (~7.5 B/ns per SM), with both generic and mapa/ld.shared::cluster addressing; the same bytes from L2 take ~380 ns, so cluster exchange of bulk data loses on RTX PRO 6000

gemv_chain_summary.reading: Static tiles: every SM waits a mean 6.6-11 us per boundary for the slowest SM (DRAM service is uneven across SMs and tiles are 21 or 22 rows), so the exposed cost (1.2-2.3 us with the ring continuing across the boundary, 2.8-3.2 us drained) is dominated by stragglers, not by the 1.2 us gather; a 12-row ring barely helps. Dynamic row claiming (rows taken from a per-GEMV atomic as ring slots free, claims running into the next GEMV, LL8 per-row outputs) removes the straggler: exposed 0.99-1.06 us vs its own stream-only kernel, 0.74-0.80 us vs the static stream-only kernel.

conclusions.best_designs: fp32: LL16 flag-in-data with 8 replicas (1,151 ns); bf16: single counter (red arrive, ld.acquire poll) with the vector written to 8 replicas (1,004 ns). Nothing beat the single counter for the signal itself: per-producer flags (2.2-2.6 us), sharded counters (1.29-1.69 us with data) and cluster hierarchies (1.6-1.9 us) all add polling traffic or a cluster barrier.
conclusions.megatron_pair: one all-reduce of 4096 fp32 costs 3,645 ns (red.add) / 3,715 ns (LL16 two hops) / 5,581 ns (cluster DSMEM) vs 2 x 1,151 = 2,302 ns for the two gathers it replaces: on this GPU the column/row pair is slower, because the reduction moves 188 partial vectors (3 MiB) instead of 188 slices.
conclusions.recommendation: Do NOT lower the per-boundary charge below 663 ns for an all-SM dependency. 663 ns is the signal alone; moving the activation to every SM makes the isolated gather 1.0 us (bf16) to 1.15 us (fp32) at best, and under a DRAM-bound weight stream the exposed cost is 0.74-1.06 us per boundary with dynamic row scheduling and 1.2-2.3 us with static tiles. Charge ~1.0 us per all-SM boundary (range 0.74-1.15 us) for a well-built megakernel; keep 371 ns only for a one-to-one handoff that moves a few lines.
